acceptance: Accepted step exit codes can no longer silently abort preflight: either step returns 0 for an accepted outcome, or a test enforces that every --ok-codes caller maps its codes, as the owner chose.
context: Filed 2026-11-22 while closing out the run-timeout follow-ups (umbrella run-timeout-plan-20261120). Evidence was read on 2026-11-22; re-read run logs, file paths and line numbers before acting.
description:
## Problem
`scripts/preflight_receipt.py step --ok-codes 0,5` records a step as `passed` when the command exits with an accepted code, and returns the child's raw code. `test_pytest_exit_five_is_a_pass_with_its_raw_code` (`tests/unit/scripts/test_preflight_receipt.py`) pins that contract on purpose. Every caller must therefore map accepted codes itself: in `make/pr-landing.mk` the `lint-markers` step appends `|| [ "$$?" -eq 5 ]`, the `pytest` step stores the status and maps 5 to 0 (using the raw 5 to print "Mapped tests are all deselected by the default markers."), and `scripts/linux_preflight_pytest.sh` maps 5 as well. A new step that passes `--ok-codes` but forgets the mapping aborts preflight although its receipt says passed; this happened during #4443 (fixed there by adding the `||` clause).

## Change
Make the contract hard to misuse: either (a) `step` exits 0 on an accepted outcome and exposes the raw code another way (for example in its output or a flag), with the pytest step's message kept; or (b) keep the raw code, document it in `step --help`, and add a test that every `--ok-codes` caller in `make/` and `scripts/` maps its accepted codes.

## Decision gates
- STOP and ask the owner (choice dialog) between (a) and (b): (a) rewrites a test that pins the current contract on purpose.
- Do not change which outcomes count as passed, `unverified` or failed, or the receipt's required steps.

## Verification rubric
Pass, under (a): a test shows `step --ok-codes 0,5` on an exit-5 command returns 0 and records `passed`, failing before the change; the `||`/status special cases are removed; the all-deselected message still prints. Under (b): a test that enumerates every `--ok-codes` caller fails on a caller without the mapping (shown failing on a deliberately broken copy) and passes on the tree. Either way `tests/unit/scripts/test_pr_preflight_base.py` and the receipt tests pass.
Fail: callers still silently depend on remembering the mapping.

## Guardrails
Work in a linked worktree (`make worktree-create`), never the primary clone. Edit files with the edit tool, never by script. Heavy work (benchmarks, test tiers, UAT, generators at scale) only through `make heavy-run` or lock-taking entry points; never skip the lock, admission or watchdog; never delete anything under `~/Developer/benchmark_runs`. No live cloud run and no cloud credentials unless this item's Decision gates say the owner approved it in the current task. BenchBox imposes no default run limit: add none. No comments or docstrings in first-party code; one changelog fragment for a user-facing change. Never post a stand-in review, close and reopen a pull request to restart CI, use `--no-verify`, force-push, or rewrite an author. Arm once; a second time only after fixing the cause the refusal named. Reply on every review thread; resolve it only after the bot's review of the new head does not raise it again.
